title: decisio's vLLM plugin, both model classes and the patch series verified on a card
hardware: 1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (96 GB)

software.vllm: 0.30.0 (a second environment with stock vLLM 0.30.0 for the bench)
software.patch_series: applied; VLLM_SUFFIX_STAGING=1 except in the bench's off and stock cells
software.patch_series_flag_note: the flag was named VLLM_R9_SUFFIX_STAGING when this run was made; its logs keep that name

code.state: the private repository at 9f23401 with the three fixes below applied on the box; the fixed code is what this repository ships

fixes.1: register() also enters each class in vLLM's per-architecture config map (MODELS_CONFIG_MAP) with the stock text class's hook; without it the text-only class ran 544-token blocks and 50 of 1,400 suite answers matched
fixes.2: the hidden state is read in chunks of at most 1,024 allowed ids (vLLM 0.30.0's sampler limit; an oversized request killed the engine)
fixes.3: the chunks are sent one at a time and the head's label logits are recomputed in bf16 (identical requests in one batch were not the same forward; see EVAL_CARD.md)

servers.HI: H beside the image engine on the same card (0.47 and 0.49 of its memory)

gates.text-only class: pass: 1,400 of 1,400 suite answers bit-identical to V (after fix 1), C2-C4 pass
gates.hidden readout, part 3 (no change elsewh: pass: 1,400 of 1,400 bit-identical to V, three times; C2-C4 pass
gates.hidden readout, part 2 (same forward): pass: label probabilities recomputed from the recovered state within 3.1e-8 of the engine's own on 250 of 250 intent items, same option on all (after fixes 2 and 3)
gates.hidden readout, part 1 (exact arithmetic: pass: 6 of 6 stored fits equal the reference fit of their registration readout; 750 of 750 served head answers equal apply_intent_head on their own readout

round12_intent_head_accuracy.protocol: 10 labelled training examples per intent registered through POST /v1/tasks; 150 and 100 test items

results.co_residence: H and the image engine start together (33.31 and 34.23 GiB of weights); same-forward check passes on 40 items

batch_forward_finding.rows_of_one_batch: identical requests sent in one batch differed in label probability by up to 0.59 (median 0.029; diag_same_row.json)
batch_forward_finding.sequential_singletons: the same requests sent one at a time agreed to 1.2e-7, and with the text path to 6e-8 (diag_same_row_sequential.json)
batch_forward_finding.float64_vs_bf16: label logits recomputed in float64 differ from the engine's by up to 0.019 in probability; rounded to bf16 they agree within 3e-8 (diag_same_forward.json)

files.suite_<server>.json.gz: the 1,400 suite answers per server (probabilities in option order, the choice as an index; the private suite's text is not included)
files.same_forward*.json: gate part 2 per item (run 2 is the failed run before fix 3, kept on record)
files.r12/<task>_d<draw>.json: round 12 per item: gold, path, served probabilities, the recovered readout
files.r12/<task>_d0_task.json, latency_tasks.j: the stored task records (calibration and head) as GET /v1/tasks?full=1 returns them
files.latency.json.gz: per request: condition, group, server and wall milliseconds
files.health_*.json, memory_*.txt: each server's /health and its engine's memory lines

excluded: item text of any benchmark (Decision Index payloads, JevBench raw requests and responses)
Jev's published board figures, and any Jev output
vLLM start-up logs, box logs and addresses
the registration examples' hidden states (r12 *_examples.npz, 31 MB; their fits and every served answer are in r12/)
the private suite's items and round 12's item texts
